rhoswen.title: Commoner Tea
rhoswen.text:
You find Rhoswen on the back porch after dusk. She has a chipped mug of cheap street tea balanced on her knee, and her leather notebook is open beside her.

Her silver circlet is on the table. You have never seen it off her head before. Her long ears flick toward you when the screen door creaks.

"I bought it from the cart at the docks," she announces, with enormous pride. She holds up a crumpled paper bag of fried dough as evidence. "I stood in a queue. A man with a fish told me to hurry up."

She looks delighted about the man with the fish.

"At court, tea takes forty minutes and three spoons, and one may not speak until the second pouring. Out here you simply hold the cup while it's warm." She picks up her pen. "May I write down that it tastes better? I want to be accurate, and I suspect I'm biased. Nobody is watching how I hold it."
ngpp: Her pointed ears twitch faintly as you step onto the porch, as though she half-expected the exact weight of your footstep on that loose plank.
"Strange," she murmurs, glancing from the dockside pastry bag to your face. "I reached for cheap fried dough on pure instinct, as though someone once convinced me it was worth a kingdom."
"Look at me sitting barefoot with dockside tea," Rhoswen says softly, emerald eyes searching yours. "My notebook is blank, yet I swear we have shared this exact quiet porch a lifetime ago, Sam."

choices.label: Sit beside her and share the paper bag
choices.res: She breaks the pastry in half with spotless etiquette, licks sugar off her thumb, and immediately looks horrified at herself before laughing softly when you pretend not to notice.

choices.label: Call her "miss" and ask what else is in the notebook
choices.res: The tips of her ears pinken immediately. "Miss Rhoswen," she tests aloud, smiling down at her pages. "You have no idea how light two syllables can sound."

image.comp: sitting on a wooden back porch step at dusk holding a chipped mug and a paper pastry bag, open notebook beside her, pink ears, pleased smile
image.setting: quiet wooden back porch overlooking a cobblestone lane at dusk

rhoswen.title: Margin Notes
rhoswen.text:
You knock once on the washroom door, more or less, and push it open.

Rhoswen is kneeling beside the steaming tub. Her hair is pinned up in a hurry. She has a towel around her and a wet sleeve in one hand, and with the other she's holding a page of her journal up to the lamp and squinting at it.

She freezes. The towel slips an inch off one pale shoulder. Her eyes go wide.

"I dropped it in the bathwater," she says weakly. She sounds like someone caught at treason. "I was making a note about the soap. The ink under 'Propriety' has run straight into 'Breakfast'."

She turns the page toward you, to show you. It's true. Two hundred years of training are warring in her face with the fact that she's on her knees in a towel.

"I had rather a lot written under 'Propriety'," she adds. "I don't think I can read any of it now."

1.text:
You open the washroom door. Rhoswen is sitting on the rim of the bath with her damp hair pinned high. When she hears your step, she sets her soaked notebook down on the stool, out of harm's way.

Her towel slides off one shoulder. She lets it stay where it has fallen. The tips of her ears are pink, and her eyes are warm.

"Propriety appears to be ruined already," she says softly. "I've decided not to mourn it." She turns her bare shoulder toward you. "Would you help me dry my back, Sam? I find I would like to be touched by someone who isn't a lady's maid."

choices.label: Step into the steam and trace dry warmth across her shoulders
choices.res: Her pointed ears flush scarlet as her head tilts gently back into your palm.

choices.label: Pass her a dry towel and tease her about wet ink
choices.res: "I shall switch to charcoal tomorrow," she retorts softly, smiling after you.

3.text:
You push the washroom door open. Rhoswen is rising out of the steaming tub, and she isn't in any hurry about it.

Water runs down her pale skin, over her small breasts and the curve of her hips. Her wet hair clings to her neck. Her ears have gone bright rose at the tips. She picks up the towel, looks at it, and lays it over the chair.

"No notebook today," she whispers. She holds out one wet hand to you. "I've written enough about what humans do. Come into the water and do it to me. I want to learn with my body what it's like."

choices.label: Bolster the latch and join her inside the bath
choices.res: She exhales softly as you pull her bare, slick waist against you beneath the hot water.

choices.label: Wrap her in warm linen and kiss down her throat
choices.res: She shivers in the damp towel, fingers tangling straight into your collar.

choices.label: Apologize and step back out
choices.res: "Thank you!" she squeaks behind the closing latch. Ten minutes later she sets a dry towel neatly by your door with a tiny pressed leaf tucked underneath.

choices.label: Hold a towel out from the doorway
choices.res: She accepts the dry linen without rushing to cover herself, her ears turning rose as your eyes linger. "For scholarly completeness," she murmurs, "you look very steady when startled."

else.res: She snatches the towel through a two-inch crack in the door with brisk courtly dignity, though you hear her smother a flustered laugh inside.

choices.label: Tease her about waterproof ink
choices.res: "Elven ink doesn't run," she replies stiffly, clutching the towel. "Human ink is apparently much bolder." Her smile gives her away before the door clicks shut.

image.comp: kneeling beside a steaming wooden tub wrapped in a towel, holding up a wet ink-streaked notebook with bright pink ears

rhoswen.title: Unplanned Hours
rhoswen.text:
It's late, and the parlor is quiet. Rhoswen has spread half a dozen town maps and scraps of ledger across the low table. She's sitting on the rug. Her shoes are off, for once, and her heels are tucked up under her skirt.

Her notebook is beside her. She hasn't written a line in it all evening.

She's been watching you sort receipts by lamplight. Her chin has come down, a little at a time, to rest on her folded arms.

"I spent two centuries in a silver tower," she says softly. "I had a tutor for deportment and another for conversation. Nobody in all that time asked me what I thought of the weather. Nobody let me sit on a rug without correcting how I sat."

Her toes curl against the wool.

"I've been here for an hour doing nothing at all. I'm not improving myself, and I'm not being observed. I had no idea that quiet could feel so greedy. I keep wanting more of it."

choices.label: Set the receipts aside and sit on the rug beside her
choices.res: She shifts without hesitation so her shoulder rests against yours. After ten quiet minutes she turns a blank page in her notebook and writes only the date.

choices.label: Ask what she wants to do tomorrow—no notes allowed
choices.res: She thinks seriously for a whole minute. "Walk through the fish market at noon. Eat something sticky with both hands. And hold your sleeve when the crowd pushes."

image.comp: sitting barefoot on a parlor rug beside a low table strewn with maps and receipts, chin resting on folded arms, warm lamplight
image.setting: quiet parlor rug by warm hearthlight late at night

rhoswen.title: The Courier's Seal
rhoswen.text:
An elven courier in silver-trimmed livery is waiting in the entryway. He has a scroll, and the wax on it carries the stag crest of her house.

Rhoswen reads it once, in silence. You watch her spine go back into its court lines, one vertebra at a time. Her knuckles whiten on the parchment.

Her father has learned where she works. There's a carriage. It leaves at dawn. If she's on it, her name can still be scrubbed from the scandal sheets, and the matter will never be spoken of.

There's no "or" in the letter. In two hundred years, he has never needed to write one.

The courier steps outside to wait for her answer.

Rhoswen turns to you. She's calm, and the calm is thin enough to see through.

"I should not bring trouble to your door," she says. "He's a patient man, and he has a long reach. I knew that when I walked out. I'd let myself forget it, here."
ngpp: Even before breaking her father's stag seal, her chin lifts instinctively—almost like she already spoke her refusal once before.
"Weird," she murmurs, twisting the torn parchment ribbon. "My chest does not even hesitate. Why does this silver livery look smaller to me than it used to?"
"Two centuries of high-court fear," she breathes softly, turning the crest over in steady fingers. "And my heart already knows which doorway is home before you speak, Sam."

choices.label: "Stay only if you want to—this house can handle scandal."
choices.res: Some of the ice leaves her shoulders at once. She breaks the wax seal cleanly in half and hands it back to the waiting courier with a polite, devastating smile.

choices.label: "Go back if that's what makes you safe."
choices.res: Her lips thin. "Safe is what I left behind," she answers quietly—then goes out alone to send the courier away empty-handed anyway.

choices.label: Say nothing and let her choose
choices.res: She waits one heartbeat for a word that doesn't come, turns on her heel, and deals with the courier herself—returning pale and silent for the rest of the night.

image.comp: holding a silver-sealed parchment scroll, rigid aristocratic posture masking worry, emerald eyes glancing toward him

rhoswen.title: The Unfinished Margin
rhoswen.text:
After midnight, Rhoswen brings you up to the terrace garden above the square. She's carrying two glasses of pale elven wine. She's also carrying the battered leather notebook.

She hands it to you, open.

It isn't open at Human Customs. It's open near the end. The last twenty pages are full, in her tiny, careful hand, and none of them are about the town.

They're about you. She's noted how you check on the staff when they're tired. She has a sketch of the crooked angle of your hoodie pocket. She has recorded every time you remembered how she takes her tea without being told, with the date.

"I stopped studying the town months ago," she admits. Her ears are glowing crimson in the moonlight. "I told myself it was a case study. One subject, observed closely." She takes a rather large sip of the wine. "I was never very impartial. A proper scholar would have noticed by the third page."

choices.label: Kiss her hand and promise not to read ahead
choices.res: She catches her breath as your lips brush her knuckles, then closes the notebook with one slow finger. "You may read as far as you like."

choices.label: Shut the notebook and take her straight back to your bedroom
choices.res: Wine glasses stay abandoned on the parapet as her trembling smile breaks into an eager nod.

choices.label: Ask what comes on the next page
choices.res: She steps inside your reach, tilting her chin up with a bold, trembling smile. "I was hoping we might draft it together."

image.comp: standing on a moonlit terrace holding out a worn leather notebook and two wine glasses, blushing deeply down to her pointed ears
image.setting: moonlit terrace garden overlooking lantern-lit rooftops at night

rhoswen.title: Beyond the Text
rhoswen.text:
In the quiet room at the end of the hall, Rhoswen unclasps her silver circlet. She sets it down on the bedside table, beside her closed notebook.

There are no pages open tonight, and no pen in reach. She has taken the pins out, and her platinum hair is loose over her bare shoulders. She steps into your arms. She's steady, and she means it.

"I left a court because every day there had been written for me before I was born," she says against your mouth. "I knew whom I'd marry, and what I would say at the wedding."

Her hands slide up behind your neck.

"I came here to observe. I've filled a book. You're the only chapter in it I have never wanted to correct." She draws back just far enough to look at you. "I told my father's courier no. I would like to belong somewhere I chose, Sam. Let it be here, with you."
ngpp: Even setting her silver circlet aside tonight carries an uncanny rhythm, like muscle memory returning from a dream.
"Strange," she whispers against your collarbone, "I unclasped this crown as if I had sworn off marble courts for you once already."
"Whatever goddess rewrote our pages," Rhoswen breathes into your mouth, holding you fast, "she couldn't erase the warmth of this room. Stay my unwritten chapter forever, Sam."
rhoswen.goLead: You draw Rhoswen back onto the pillows, and her platinum hair fans out across your wrists. None of her court manners survive the first slow kiss.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.res: Rhoswen draws back slowly, smoothing her skirts with shaken composure. "Then I shall exercise patience," she murmurs, touching your cheek once. "I am an elf—I have plenty, even if my heart disagrees."
